review_notes: I read the whole file and the supporting B1MoreSevenB lemmas (commSub_inv_H, sup_commSub_inv, commSub_sup_le_self, mem_stabSub_of_invariant, centSec_conj). I looked for repeated nontrivial reasoning across I_le_Xplus, W_eq, W_inv_A, stab_trivial_mod and fixes_of_trivial_mod. The two closure_induction proofs (W_inv_A and hfix) use different predicates, so I did not count them. The clearest case is the fact commSub W H = W for W = I ⊔ I', which is proved twice with the same ingredients. A smaller second case is the repeated H-conjugation step for centSec. I did not compile the proposed rewrites, and the lemma name W_comm is new.

findings.excerpt: have hWc : I ⊔ I.map a.toMonoidHom ≤ commSub (I ⊔ I.map a.toMonoidHom) H := sup_le hIc hI'c
findings.problem: W_eq and fixes_of_trivial_mod each re-prove the same fact: for W = I ⊔ I.map a, the subgroup [W,H] equals W. Both start from the same two `obtain`s of `mem_irrPlus_top_iff` on `P.hI` and `P.irr'`. Both then derive `W ≤ commSub W H` from `commI`, `commI'` and `commSub_mono le_sup_left/right le_rfl`. W_eq spells this out as `hIc`, `hI'c` and `hWc`. fixes_of_trivial_mod does it in one line with `▸`. The reverse inclusion `commSub W H ≤ W` is `commSub_le_of_invariant (isInv_sup invI invI')`. W_eq uses it at the end of its second `calc` step, and fixes_of_trivial_mod uses it as the first half of `hWc`. So the full equality is proved in two places and never stated as a lemma.
findings.proposed_change:
Before `W_eq`, add
`theorem W_comm (P : B72Hyp H A a I) : commSub (I ⊔ I.map a.toMonoidHom) H = I ⊔ I.map a.toMonoidHom`.
Proof sketch: obtain `invI, commI` and `invI', commI'` from `mem_irrPlus_top_iff`. Then `le_antisymm (commSub_le_of_invariant (isInv_sup invI invI')) (sup_le (commI ▸ commSub_mono le_sup_left le_rfl) (commI' ▸ commSub_mono le_sup_right le_rfl))`. This is the existing code from lines 159–161.
In W_eq, replace `hIc`, `hI'c` and `hWc` with `P.W_comm.ge`. Replace the final `commSub_le_of_invariant (isInv_sup invI invI')` with `P.W_comm.le`. W_eq then needs only `obtain ⟨-, -, -, -⟩` or no obtains at all.
In fixes_of_trivial_mod, replace the `hWc` block (lines 159–161) with `have hWc := P.W_comm`. The `commI`, `commI'` binders in that proof can be dropped. `invI` and `invI'` stay for `hWH`.
findings.benefit: The identity [W,H]=W is stated and proved once under its natural hypotheses. W_eq loses about 7 lines of set-up and fixes_of_trivial_mod loses its re-derivation. A later change to how perfectness of the irreducible summands is stored then needs one edit.

findings.problem: Inside fixes_of_trivial_mod, the same argument is written out twice: conjugating an element of `centSec W Z` by an element of H stays in `centSec W Z`. It needs three ingredients. The first is W-invariance of g and g⁻¹ (via `mem_stabSub_of_invariant`). The second is the fact that g fixes Z pointwise (`hz g hg`). The third is `centSec_conj`. `hNn` does this for `g * n * g⁻¹` (lines 172–177). `hbn` does it again for `h * b * h⁻¹` with `hhs` and `hbc` (the `centSec_conj hbc hhs (fun z hz => by rw [hz h hh]; exact hz)` call near line 205). The ingredients are rebuilt each time.
findings.proposed_change:
After `hWH`, add one local fact:
`have hconj : ∀ g ∈ H, ∀ n ∈ centSec W Z, g * n * g⁻¹ ∈ centSec W Z := fun g hg n hn => centSec_conj hn (mem_stabSub_of_invariant (hWH g hg) (hWH g⁻¹ (H.inv_mem hg))) (fun z hz => by rw [hz g hg]; exact hz)`.
Then `hNn` becomes `⟨H.mul_mem (H.mul_mem hg hn.1) (H.inv_mem hg), hconj g hg n hn.2⟩`. The second component of `hbn` becomes `(centSec W Z).mul_mem (hconj h hh b hbc) ((centSec W Z).inv_mem hbc)`, and `hhs` is no longer needed.
findings.benefit: This removes the duplicated invariance bookkeeping and makes it clear that both uses rely on the same fact. It is a smaller gain than the first finding, because the repeated code is only a few lines and stays inside one proof.
